newsitem.title: USA: Fidelity to relocate fixed income, money mkts to NH.
newsitem.headline: Fidelity to relocate fixed income, money mkts to NH.

text.p: Fidelity Investments Monday said it plans to relocate its fixed-income and money market investment management divisions to the company's regional operating center in Merrimack, N.H.

In December, Fidelity began to make preparations to consolidate the new divisions in one location. The money market group had been in Dallas and the fixed-income group was in Boston. This fall, both groups will be under one roof with a state-of-the-art trading floor and the latest technology, Fidelity said.
About 330 employees will work in the two groups and related support functions, bringing Fidelity's total employment in Merrimack to about 1,700.
Fidelity also announced some portfolio manager changes that will result because Steve Harvey, Janice Bradburn and Leland Barron have indicated they did not wish to relocate to the new site.

Effective April 1, the following changes will occur: George A. Fischer, Jonathan D. Short, Norman Lind and David L. Murphy will be taking over municipal bond funds currently managed by Steven W. Harvey; Diane McLaughlin and Scott Orr will be taking over municipal money market funds currently managed by Janice Bradburn; and Robert A. Litterst will take over taxable money market funds currently managed by Leland C. Barron.
Fidelity Investments is the nation's largest mutual fund company and one of the leading providers of financial services.
